sources.citation: OLAC: 'OLAC resources in and about the Gowlan language' (ISO 639-3 goj), listing as of 2023-03-09, plus item record oai:sil.org:90546 (Internet Archive copy).
sources.note: Bibliographic only: the sole non-catalogue resource for goj is Stahl 2021 (sociolinguistics).

sources.citation: SIL Language & Culture Archives record 90546 (Stahl 2021), Internet Archive copy 2024-07-23; used to locate the PDF and read the abstract.

Stahl, James L. 2021 [fieldwork 1984-1986]. A Sociolinguistic Survey of the Korku [kfq] Language Area. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2021-040. Dallas: SIL International. 102 pp. (OLAC subject languages kfq, goj, gok; the only OLAC-listed work on Gowlan besides Glottolog/Ethnologue.)
sources.note: Nothing. Purely sociolinguistic (bilingualism, attitudes, language use of the Gowlans of Chikli, Dharni taluk: secs 4.2.2, 5.2.2, 6.2.2, 7.2.3). States only that Gowlis and Gowlans 'speak languages belonging to the Indo-Aryan language family' (p.1). Appendix F wordlists (page scan) cover Korku dialects and Nihali only; no Gowlan wordlist, no phonology, no mention of stress/accent.
sources.venue: A Sociolinguistic Survey of the Korku [kfq] Language Area

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul, Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2016. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 19th ed., entry 'Gowlan' [goj]. Dallas: SIL International. (Internet Archive copy)
sources.note: Nothing. Gives pop. 20,200 (2000), Amravati dt. among Korku and Hoshangabad dt; 'Indo-Aryan, Outer Languages, Southern, Unclassified'; 'May be more similar to Hindi (Central zone) than to Marathi (Southern zone)'; 'Belong to Gowli caste'.

sources.citation: Russell, R. V. & Hira Lal. 1916. The Tribes and Castes of the Central Provinces of India, vol. III, article 'Gaoli'. London: Macmillan.
sources.note: Older ethnography of the Gaoli of Berar/Nimar/Hoshangabad; may name the dialect they speak (identity only). Full view on archive.org but not downloaded (search engines and IA search unavailable by automated download at check time).

sources.citation: Hammarström, Forkel, Haspelmath & Bank. Glottolog 5.x languoid gowl1242 'Gowlan' (bookkeeping; md.ini and web/JSON record).
sources.note: Nothing; zero descriptive references; no retirement comment beyond the generic bookkeeping note; hh classification tag 'Masica: Indo-Aryan / Kogan: New Indo-Aryan'.

sources.citation: Wikipedia 'Gowlan language' (redirects to Gowari people) and Wikidata Q12953532 'Bhalay-Gowlan'.
sources.note: Nothing; no linguistic content; Wikidata label pairs the name with 'Bhalay', another caste speech form Stahl lists separately.

sources.citation: Devy, G. N. (gen. ed.) / Jakhade, Arun (vol. ed.). 2013-2017. People's Linguistic Survey of India, Maharashtra volume(s) (The Languages of Maharashtra). Hyderabad: Orient BlackSwan. Possible entry on Gavli/Gawli boli of Melghat.

sources.note: PLSI state volumes carry short community-language sketches, sometimes with a phonology paragraph; the only plausible place a first-hand note on Gowlan/Gawli-boli sound structure might exist. Existence of such an entry not verified.

sources.citation: Hammarström, Harald. 2015. Ethnologue 16/17/18th editions: A comprehensive review: online appendices. Language 91(3). Entry for Gowlan [goj].

sources.note: Would state why Glottolog treats Gowlan as a bookkeeping/undemonstrated language and whether any wordlist or description was ever located; settles identity (which Indo-Aryan language the Melghat Gowli actually speak), not stress.

sources.citation: Singh, K. S. (ed.). 2004. People of India: Maharashtra (Anthropological Survey of India, vol. XXX, 3 parts). Mumbai: Popular Prakashan. Entries 'Gaoli/Gawli' and 'Bhalay'.
